Lenses
How JavaScript lenses read and update nested data without mutation: view, set and over from Ramda, and your own lens built from a getter and a setter.
Learn to read and update nested data with lenses (view, set, over) without changing the original object, and understand how a simple lens built from a getter and a setter works.
text
Lenses are a tool (a pattern) used in functional programming when working with data, providing data immutability and function purity.
Immutability means that data does not change after it is created: instead of modifying it, you create a new copy with the changes applied.

And now let's try to implement our own custom lens. In production code, use ready-made solutions such as the lenses in Ramda JS (Sanctuary JS has no lenses).
Lenses are a pattern for working with data that keeps the data immutable and the functions pure.
view reads the value at the lens path, set writes a new value and returns a new object, and over works like set but takes a function of the current value. The original data stays unchanged.
A simple lens can be built from a pair of getter and setter functions closed over the path to the data; when a node is copied, an array has to be copied as an array.
In production code, use ready-made lenses such as the ones in Ramda; Sanctuary has no lenses.

The application state holds the user's settings and a cart. Using R.lensPath, R.view, R.set and R.over, get a new state where the theme is dark and the quantity of the first item in the cart has gone up by one. Combine both changes into a single update function with pipe and make sure the original state has not changed.

new: theme dark, quantity 2
original: theme light, quantity 1

In the hand-written lens from the lesson, set cannot store a function as a value: the setter treats any function as a transformation. Write a lens lensKey(key) for a single object key whose setter always takes a function, plus view, over and set. Build set on top of over, as Ramda does, and check that a function is stored as a plain value and the original object does not change.
